title: HDRTransDC: High Dynamic Range Image Reconstruction with Transformer Deformation Convolution

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Text references Table 1 (quantitative comparison), Table 2 (inference time), and Table 3 (ablation) multiple times, but no table content exists anywhere in the paper — all quantitative claims (e.g., 'outperforms Liu by 0.34 dB PSNR-μ') are unverifiable from the paper itself. The original arXiv paper (2403.06831) was withdrawn by its authors citing 'potential problems in metric calculation in Sections 4.2 and 4.3' — exactly the sections whose supporting tables are missing.

13 figure placeholders (Figures 0, 11–22) exist in the paper but are never referenced in the text. The original source paper (arXiv 2403.06831) contains only Figures 1–10. These extra figures appear to be extraction artifacts or injected content with no counterpart in the source document.

'Caused by large motion and severe under-/over-exposure among input LDR images, HDR imaging suffers from ghosting artifacts and fusion distortions.' — dangling modifier: HDR imaging is not caused by motion; the ghosting/fusion artifacts are. Missing proper subject for the cause clause (should be 'Due to large motion...').

'In the under-/over-exposed regions where seriously miss the information, inaccurate information recovery leads to fusion distortions...' — missing subject in the relative clause; should be 'where information is seriously missing' or equivalent.

Two consistent terminology drifts: (1) Module name alternates between 'Deformable' (Abstract/Intro) and 'Deformation' (Section 3.1 heading) — the network is 'Transformer Deformation Convolution' but the module fluctuates. (2) 'fusion distortions' (Abstract, Method) vs 'fusing distortions' (Intro, Method, Conclusion) are used interchangeably throughout.

Section 3 states 'The resolution of images is 1000 × 1500' while Section 4.3 states 'generating 15 images with the resolution of 1500 × 1000'. Same dimensions transposed (width/height swapped) for the same Kalantari dataset. External sources confirm 1000×1500 is correct.

Eq (3) labels the attention as 'multi-headed self-attention (MSA)' but Eq (2) defines Q from reference tokens and K/V from non-reference tokens — this is cross-attention, not self-attention. The paper's own narrative confirms this: 'we search for features similar to the reference image on the non-reference image.'

Abstract and Conclusion claim 'state-of-the-art performance' but the experiments text quantifies superiority against only a single baseline (Liu et al. 2022) by ≤0.34 dB. The full comparison table (Table 1) is not present in text. No comparison with transformer-based methods from 2022-2023 or diffusion-based HDR methods. The paper was withdrawn by authors citing metric calculation problems in the comparison sections.

Paper (submitted March 2024) reviews no work newer than 2022 and misses highly relevant prior art: ADNet (CVPRW 2021 — deformable convolution for HDR alignment, the paper's claimed novelty mechanism); Selective TransHDR (ECCV 2022 — transformer-based selective HDR); SCTNet (ICCV 2023 — alignment-free transformer); DiffHDR (TCSVT 2023 — first diffusion-based HDR deghosting, public ~4 months before submission).

Oh et al. listed as TPAMI 2014 but official publication is June 2015 (Vol. 37, No. 6). Zhang & Cham listed as TIP 2011 but official publication is April 2012 (Vol. 21, No. 4). Both use early-access/DOI year instead of official issue year; volume/page numbers are correct.

'The estimated HDR image contains the similar structure as the reference image.' — ungrammatical collocation; should be 'has a structure similar to the reference image' or 'contains the same structure as'.
'our method outperforms the exiting Liu's method' — typo: 'exiting' should be 'existing'.

Debevec & Malik's 'Recovering High Dynamic Range Radiance Maps from Photographs' was originally published at SIGGRAPH 1997, not 2008. The paper cites the 2008 SIGGRAPH classes reprint, which is bibliographically self-consistent but misleading on the work's actual vintage.

Several key parameters are never specified: M (local Transformer layers), N (global Transformer layers), number of stacked TDCAM modules, number of RDWFB blocks, deformable convolution kernel count K, local Transformer window size, and DWFB attention block φ details. The symbols are used consistently but never concretized — a reproducibility gap.

Adam β1=0.5 is non-standard (typically 0.9 in the PyTorch default and in all cited reference papers). Stated only once in Section 3 with no justification. Not an error per se but a notable deviation from convention.

Inconsistent reference style: 'as shown in Fig. 5(a)' vs 'As shown in 5(b), we build the RDWFB...' — the second drops the 'Fig.' prefix. Also 'the red block in Figure 6 and 7' should be 'Figures 6 and 7'.

'It is confirmed that the LDR images are effective in detecting saturated and noisy regions and HDR domains are effective in detecting moving objects.' — assertive framing ('It is confirmed') with no citation attached. The claim traces to Kalantari et al. 2017 (acknowledged in context via 'Following previous work') but the phrasing presents a borrowed observation as established fact.

summary:
The paper HDRTransDC proposes a transformer-based deformable convolution network for HDR image reconstruction. Verification across 5 dimensions (math, text, figures, citations, cross-section consistency) on 38 snippets found 16 detected errors across multiple categories. 

CRITICAL FINDINGS: (1) Tables 1–3, containing all quantitative evidence for the paper's core SOTA claims, are entirely missing from the document — every numerical comparison (PSNR, SSIM, HDR-VDP-2 deltas) is unverifiable from the paper itself. The original arXiv version (2403.06831) was withdrawn by its authors citing 'potential problems in metric calculation in Sections 4.2 and 4.3.' (2) 13 unreferenced figures (0, 11–22) have no counterpart in the original 10-figure source paper. (3) Terminology drifts throughout ('Deformable' vs 'Deformation', 'fusion' vs 'fusing distortions'). (4) MSA is mislabeled as self-attention when the paper defines cross-attention (Q from reference, K/V from non-reference). (5) Multiple grammatical errors in the abstract and method sections. (6) The SOTA claim is supported by comparison against only a single baseline (Liu 2022) in the text, with no discussion of 2023 transformer/diffusion-based HDR methods. (7) Key architectural hyperparameters (M, N, K, TDCAM/RDWFB counts, φ details, window sizes) are never specified, creating a significant reproducibility gap. 

POSITIVE: All 8 equations are mathematically sound with no algebraic or dimensional errors. All 25 citations correspond to real, correctly-described papers. The related work sections accurately characterize prior methods. The grammatical and formatting issues are minor but numerous. Overall verdict: NEEDS_CORRECTION — the missing tables and metric-calculation concerns in the quantitative comparison sections (which the authors themselves flagged in their arXiv withdrawal) require substantive correction before the paper's claims can be considered verified.
